editorial:
Ever wonder how one guy managed to change movies forever? You get a front-row seat to that journey here. It is not just a dry history lesson, but a cool look at George Lucas as a young filmmaker with a crazy dream. You will see how he went from a kid who loved cameras to the creator of the biggest space fantasy ever told. The vibe is very inspiring and focuses on the hard work and risks he took when nobody believed in his ideas.

What really works is the use of old footage and interviews that make the story move quickly. You will love seeing the early sketches and the mess behind the scenes of Star Wars. One downside is that it focuses mostly on the early years, so you might want more about the prequels. Still, if you love movies, you need to see this. You can find it for rent on Apple TV or just grab the Blu-ray for your physical collection if you want the best quality. It is a great pick for a rainy afternoon on your couch.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing how Lucas became one of the richest and most powerful people in Hollywood. It explains that he didn't just make a movie, but he built a whole empire of toys and sequels. The final scenes show him reflecting on his legacy and how he used his success to start a school for film. It ends with the idea that his biggest win was following his own gut feeling.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Star Wars or wants to learn about filmmaking.
